programme.desc: South of York, biker cop Joe Moisley responds to a serious collision on the A63 - a car has veered head on into oncoming traffic, colliding with two HGVs travelling the other way. He experiences the local dance and music craze known as 'Budots', which was bizarrely inspired by Duterte's 'death squads'. He later arrives in the Islamic city of Marawi, which was destroyed in a battle between Jihadists and the military. Needing a full military escort, he explores the bomb-damaged city. Arriving at the main port of Jolo, Michael sees what appears a lively and friendly island, and he reflects on a country where warmth and happiness coexist with recurring crises. programme.title: Murder Scene: The Incident Room
programme.desc: A fierce blaze tears through a bungalow in the Hampshire village of Liss. Inside, firefighters discover 96-year-old Emma Finch dead on her bedroom floor. What first appears to be a tragic accident soon feels wrong: the fire is unusually contained, key details don't add up, and detectives suspect the scene was staged. A murder inquiry is launched, but the flames have destroyed vital evidence. As detectives reconstruct Emma's final hours, digital forensics reveal a vehicle on the road, pointing to someone in Emma's inner circle. CCTV, phone data and forensic traces expose a hidden timeline - until the post-mortem reveals Emma died in a way no one expected. With only hours to act, detectives race to expose what really happened in that bedroom. Exec Prods: Andrew Sheldon/Christian Hills; Dir: Luke Rufo; True North
Inside the nerve centre of murder inquiries, revealed through the detectives themselves.

programme.title: Cause of Death
programme.desc: In March 2017, 17-year-old Derbyshire boxer Ed Bilbey - aiming to win the East Midlands amateur youth welterweight title - was passed medically fit to fight, but after just nine minutes in the ring he collapsed. Despite the efforts of paramedics and hospital staff he was pronounced dead later that evening. Neither his family, nor his young opponent, can understand why he has died. Forensic Pathologist Dr Richard Shepherd sets out to explain what could have led to the death of an athletic young boxer. The investigation into Ed's death is one that leads to an inquest where questions of responsibility lead to a change in England Boxing guidelines. But do Ed's family find the answers they seek? And in June 2023, 21-year-old Warwick University student Isaac Harris was found dead on his bed by his father. A post-mortem provides no clues, but a toxicology report reveals that Isaac's body is missing vital medication to control epileptic seizures. Could a seizure have killed him? Or is there more to his death than first appears? Exec Prod: Zoe Callan; Dir: Lee Chapman; Candour Productions (S4 Ep3)
It's a coroner's job to ensure that no one goes to their grave with questions unanswered.

programme.title: My Wife, My Killer & The Secret Footage
programme.desc: Jamie and Jennifer Faith seemed like the perfect couple. Loved by friends, family and neighbours... they had the perfect life in Dallas. Then, one morning, Jamie was brutally gunned down while a distraught Jennifer was beaten and tied up by the killer. Much of this was caught on doorbell cam, as was most of the aftermath, with Jennifer interviewed in the police cells and quizzed by reporters outside the family home, as a massive nationwide manhunt launched to catch the killer. However, all was not what it seemed. This programme combines extraordinary doorbell cam and police cell footage with emotional interviews featuring devastated friends and family, key lawyers and detectives, plus incredible material of Jennifer, the woman at the heart of this remarkable story. (Originally aired as a single episode.) Prod/Dir: Edmond Buckley; Prods: Lucy de Vaux-Balbirnie/Sarah Powell; Exec Prod: Oliver Wright; Coming Up Roses (Ep1/2)

programme.title: My Wife, My Killer & The Secret Footage
